clue.text: Following urge, go mad for drink

indicators.note: the second piece follows on from the first, so the urge comes first in the answer

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
to flip is to lose one's temper or go mad

explanation.surface: Someone gives in to a sudden craving and goes wild for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg-flip is a hot or cold drink of beaten egg with milk, beer or spirits, much like eggnog.

clue.text: Takes out trusts with heart uplifted

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifted means turned upwards, and heart limits that turning to the middle three letters of the word

parts.note: to trust that something will happen is to expect it

explanation.surface: Someone removes trust funds whose central portion has been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart uplifted' turns only the middle PEC of EXPECTS to CEP, giving EX-CEP-TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To except is to exclude or leave out, so excepts is a formal synonym for takes out.

clue.text: My kind overcomes affliction

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written over another sits above it in the grid

parts.note: kind means good, as in a good deed
grief is a form of distress or affliction

explanation.surface: A kindly nature triumphs over suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is an exclamation of surprise here, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of surprise or dismay, used interchangeably as exclamations.

clue.text: Left takeaway pancake

indicators.note: away suggests the letters of the preceding word wander off out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A pancake abandoned after being bought from a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word 'takeaway' must be read as two, 'take' and 'away', with 'away' signalling the rearrangement; the surface pictures a pancake bought from a takeaway shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A latke is a Jewish fried pancake of grated potato, traditional at Hanukkah.

clue.text: Ends up bent, my back broken by old Cinephile, for one

indicators.note: broken by means the assembled letters are split open with another piece inserted
bent here means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: back means the short word is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A film buff is left twisted and broken by something ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' rearranges ENDS UP and 'back' turns MY; 'broken by' splits the result so that O lands after the fifth letter. Cinephile is a Guardian crossword setter's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinephile is the pen name of a crossword setter, so it is an example of an assumed name.

clue.text: Cold contestant's mostly put out

indicators.note: out signals that the following letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a disputant is someone who contests an argument

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of put, dropped

explanation.surface: A competitor in a cold mood is largely annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims PUT to PU; 'out' removes PU from DISPUTANT. 'Put out' wants to be an anagram signal or 'annoyed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold manner is aloof, and distant describes a reserved, unfriendly attitude.

clue.text: In drink, finally lose hope

indicators.note: In places the selected letter inside the drink

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Drowning sorrows in drink until hope is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A dream is an aspiration or ambition, so it is a synonym for a hope.

clue.text: Servants consult brief short list, getting it wrong

indicators.note: getting it wrong signals the combined letters are muddled into a new order
brief means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
the final letter removed

indicators.note: short likewise docks the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: taken as written
the final letter removed

explanation.surface: Household staff check a short list and make a mess of it.
explanation.walkthrough: CONSUL and LIS, each cut by its own indicator, are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Scullions were kitchen servants who did menial work such as washing pots.

clue.text: Consent to a sin, but not fully

indicators.note: not fully means the word is incomplete, losing its last letter

parts.note: greed is one of the seven deadly sins
the final letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly gives permission to wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to give consent, both verbs meaning to go along with something.

clue.text: I finish on 5/4 having arranged extra day, but not 1/12

indicators.note: having arranged signals that the letters are put into a new order, with one excluded

parts.note: d was the old British penny, one twelfth of a shilling

explanation.surface: A calendar puzzle about adding a day while dropping a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not' removes D (the old penny, 1/12 of a shilling) from EXTRA DAY before rearranging. Dates are British: 5/4 is 5 April.
explanation.definitionFit: The UK tax year runs to 5 April, so it is the period that ends on that date.

clue.text: Farm company represses resistance with us

indicators.note: represses means holds something down within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
the clue appears in the Financial Times, so us is FT

explanation.surface: A firm crushes opposition with the newspaper's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' is the newspaper speaking: the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: A croft is a small rented farm, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: I've changed from business chief into farcical Brian, a lady killer

indicators.note: changed from names the letters to be replaced in the longer word
into names what those letters become

parts.note: an executive is a senior manager in a business
taken as the letters I, V, E
Brian Rix was an English actor famous for stage farces

explanation.surface: A boss reinvents herself as a comic actor turned murderess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lady killer' playfully reads executrix as a female executioner rather than a woman who administers a will.
explanation.definitionFit: An executrix is a woman who executes, here cheekily taken as one who carries out executions.

clue.text: Gaffer regularly tucked into flan, daughter making dinner for Napoleon?

indicators.note: tucked into places the picked letters inside the pastry

parts.note: a flan is an open pie

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An old man digs into a flan while his daughter cooks for a French emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is the pig who rules in Orwell's Animal Farm, not the French emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon in Animal Farm is a pig, so his food would be swill fed to swine.

clue.text: Set back admitted by chap from an island

indicators.note: admitted by puts the reversed piece inside the other

parts.note: a chap is a male

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A man lets in a group that has been sent back from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Maltese describes someone or something native to the Mediterranean island of Malta.

clue.text: Hasty sort frames wife

indicators.note: frames means surrounds like a picture frame, so the other piece goes inside

parts.note: to sift is to sort or sieve

explanation.surface: An impatient person sets up his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means quick or speedy, a near synonym for hurried.

clue.text: Fossil I lift in worn-out shell

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside another word
shell says the word acts as an outer casing around them

parts.note: trite means overused, hackneyed
to lob is to lift a ball high

explanation.surface: Someone raises a fossil from a crumbling casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilobites are extinct marine arthropods, common as fossils from the Palaeozoic era.

clue.text: This very one's certainly not on the ER cast

parts.note: no is an emphatic refusal

indicators.note: cast means thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists this person certainly does not appear in the hospital drama ER.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors of ER, but it is the rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase emphasises identity, meaning the very person or thing just mentioned.

clue.text: Ultimately win by an unusually remote distance

indicators.note: Ultimately picks the final letter of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: A victory by a surprisingly wide margin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanometre is a billionth of a metre, a unit of length or distance.

clue.text: Retreat from chap about to break into explosive anger

parts.note: HE stands for high explosive

indicators.note: to break into means the turned piece is inserted into the other word

parts.note: rage is fury or anger

indicators.note: about means the name is turned round

parts.note: Tim is a man's name, standing for any chap

explanation.surface: A man retreats from someone about to burst into furious temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosive anger' looks like an anagram, but 'explosive' gives HE (high explosive); 'about' turns TIM into MIT, which breaks into HE RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage is a secluded dwelling, a place of retreat from the world.

clue.text: Smell held back in silence by an itinerant vendor

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the other

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum

indicators.note: held back means the word is reversed

parts.note: niff is British slang for a bad smell
taken as written

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman keeps quiet about an odour.
explanation.walkthrough: The muffin man was a street seller of muffins in old London, known from the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The muffin man was a hawker who walked the streets selling muffins.

clue.text: Threatens capture of English knight with his weapons?

indicators.note: capture of means the outer word takes the other pieces prisoner inside it

parts.note: maces were heavy clubs carried by knights
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Seizing an Englishman, a knight brandishes his arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace is to threaten, so menaces is a synonym for threatens.

clue.text: Band separates after a comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to part is to separate

explanation.surface: A music group splits up after a reunion.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a band of leather or fabric used to fasten or hold.

clue.text: Congratulate oneself about tactics, initially opening in double bluff

indicators.note: about means the outer word goes round the inserted letter

parts.note: to preen oneself is to be self-congratulatory

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it
opening in picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A player gloats over a ploy that begins with a double bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double bluff' looks like a single phrase; 'double' gives D and 'bluff' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff is to feign or pretend, deceiving by a false show.

clue.text: Break of service?

parts.note: a break from military service: leave for rest and recreation, abbreviated with initials, not a tennis break

explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for rest and recuperation, leave granted to service personnel.

clue.text: Bent back? On the critical list, at last

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of these words in turn

explanation.surface: Someone with a stooped back is gravely ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent back?' tempts a reversal of a word for bent; 'Bent' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Having knelt means having bent the knees, a past-tense sense of bending down.

clue.text: Park craft in tunnel for girl

indicators.note: Park means set something down in a place, starting the insertion
in says where it goes, inside the other word

parts.note: a mine is an underground tunnel
art means skill or craft

explanation.surface: Leaving a vehicle or boat in an underground passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Martine is a female given name, so it is an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Grew the ultimate in cactus flowers

parts.note: rose means increased or grew

indicators.note: the ultimate in picks the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A cactus at last produced its blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses are a popular kind of flowering shrub, so they are an example of flowers.

clue.text: Bold prisoner's prepared to go outside hideout

parts.note: a con is a convict or prisoner

indicators.note: to go outside means the word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: fit means ready or prepared
a den is a hideaway or lair

explanation.definitionFit: A confident person is self-assured, which is close to being bold.

clue.text: Prize fight ultimately has a purpose for boxing

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the picked letter goes inside

parts.note: sake means purpose, as in for the sake of

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A prize fight has a point in the boxing world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize fight' and 'boxing' form a sporting picture; 'Prize' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake is money that can be won in a contest, so it can mean a prize.

clue.text: Excess low-grade fruits go rotten

indicators.note: go rotten means the letters decay into a new order

explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an overabundance, too much of something.

clue.text: Where one's said to drive on frogs?

definitions.text: Where one's said to drive on frogs?

parts.words: Where one's said to drive on frogs?
parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang frog and toad means road, so frogs are roads in the London district famous for that slang
